3B.01.b:
### Point & say — the portals
| Portal | Where | At risk |
|---|---|---|
| **Proximal anteromedial** | 2 cm above the medial epicondyle, in front of the medial IMS (intermuscular septum) | Median nerve, MABC (medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve); ulnar nerve if it subluxes |
| **Proximal anterolateral** | 2 cm above, 1 cm in front of the lateral epicondyle | Radial nerve 7.9 mm extended / 13.7 mm at 90° (Field 1994) |
| Distal anterolateral | 3 cm below, 1 cm in front of the lateral epicondyle | Radial nerve 3.8 mm extended / 7.2 mm at 90° (Field 1994) |
| **Midlateral (soft spot)** | Lateral epicondyle · radial head · olecranon triangle | Few → first portal for distension |
| Posterolateral / direct posterior | Beside or through the triceps above the olecranon | Ulnar nerve in the medial gutter |

(Netter; Field 1994; Stothers 1995)
[[FIG: Fig 3B.2 · 3B.01

- **Distend + flex 90°** → nerves fall away; proximal portals safer than distal (Field 1994; Stothers 1995)

- Before any medial portal → feel for a **subluxing ulnar nerve** (→ 3A 3.09)

3B.02.t: Lateral Approaches I — Kocher & Modified Kocher
3B.02.b:
### Step by step
| Step | Kocher (ECU–anconeus) |
|---|---|
| Uses | Radial head, capitellum (± trochlea), lateral epicondyle, **LCL (lateral collateral ligament) repair** (Prof Mansour) |
| Position | Supine, arm across the chest, **forearm pronated** (Hopp) |
| Incision | Lateral epicondyle → posterior ulnar border 6–8 cm below the olecranon tip (Prof Mansour; Hopp 6 cm, Campbell 3–5 cm) |
| Interval | **Anconeus (radial) / ECU (extensor carpi ulnaris; PIN)** → the only true internervous lateral plane (Hopp; → 3A 3.07) |
| Superficial | Find the gap **distally**, where fibres diverge; proximally they share one aponeurosis (Hopp; Campbell) |
| Deep | Supinator + capsule → capsulotomy at the **equator of the radial head** (Prof Mansour) |

[[FIG: Fig 3B.3, 3B.4 · 3B.02

- Capsulotomy **front → PIN**, **back → LUCL** (lateral ulnar collateral ligament) (Prof Mansour)
- Annular ligament → open **1 cm in front of the ulna** to spare the LUCL (AO)

### Dangers, LCL repair & extension
| At risk | Why | Protect |
|---|---|---|
| **PIN** | Crosses the neck 2–4 cm below the head; moves with rotation (Prof Mansour) | **Full pronation**; nothing below the annular ligament; no Hohmann in front of the neck (Hopp; AO) |
| Radial nerve | Over the anterolateral capsule (Hopp) | Open the joint laterally, never anteriorly |
| **LUCL** | Lies just behind the Kocher interval (Prof Mansour) | Stay at the equator; cut and missed → **iatrogenic PLRI** (Sport sheet) → repair |

[[FIG: Fig 3B.5, 3B.6 · 3B.02

- **LUCL repair** → anchor at the **most proximal point** of the epicondyle footprint, not its centre (Prof Mansour)
- Repair it **with the extensor mass**, never the ligament alone (Prof Mansour)
- Distal extension → ≈2 cm in pronation; beyond that → **expose the PIN** (Prof Mansour)
- Extensile? → Hopp "no way to extend profitably" · Campbell "extensile"

PITFALL — how far does pronation move the PIN?
- Prof Mansour → ≈30 mm (L03), 1.5–2 cm (L05 safe zones), 2–2.5 cm (L05 summary)
- Prof Mansour table (L06) → head-to-PIN 4 cm pronated, 2.5 cm neutral, 2 cm supinated
- Say → "**pronation moves the PIN 1.5–3 cm away**; inside the joint supination gives more room" (Arrigoni 2019)

MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "approach to the radial head"
- **Kocher** → anconeus (radial) / ECU (PIN), forearm **pronated**
- Capsule at the **equator** → front = PIN, back = LUCL
- Stay **above the annular ligament**; no retractor round the neck (PIN on bone in ≈25%, Hopp)
- LCL torn (fracture-dislocation) → Kocher reaches it; LCL intact → Kaplan or EDC split spares it
- Close → repair LUCL to its isometric point (Campbell)

3B.03.t: Lateral Approaches II — Kaplan, EDC Split, Lateral Column & Boyd
3B.03.b:
### Kaplan & EDC split
| | Kaplan | EDC split |
|---|---|---|
| Interval | **ECRB / EDC** (extensor carpi radialis brevis / extensor digitorum communis) → find it **distally** (Prof Mansour) | Through the middle of EDC (Prof Mansour) |
| Incision | Lateral epicondyle → Lister's tubercle, 6–8 cm (Prof Mansour) | Same, 5–7 cm |
| Plus | **Anterior to the LUCL** → ligament safe; good view of head, coronoid, capitellum | Less PIN risk than Kaplan, less LCL risk than Kocher |
| Minus | Close to the **PIN** (≈2.5 cm, 4 cm pronated); cannot reach a torn LUCL | — |

(Prof Mansour; AO)
[[FIG: Fig 3B.7, 3B.8 · 3B.03

- AO → split the extensors at the point that **halves the capitellum** front-to-back
- Retract only **behind**; in front → ordinary retractor, never a Hohmann (PIN, radial recurrent artery) (Prof Mansour)

### Lateral column, BR–ECRL & lateral epicondyle osteotomy
| Option | Key step | Watch |
|---|---|---|
| **Lateral column** | EDC split carried 4–5 cm up the supracondylar ridge; mobile wad front, triceps back (Prof Mansour) | Radial nerve **between mobile wad and brachialis** → lift brachialis subperiosteally |
| BR–ECRL (brachioradialis–extensor carpi radialis longus) interval | PIN decompression → superficial radial nerve under BR leads up to the PIN (Prof Mansour) | Nerve to ECRB ≠ PIN (→ 3A 3.09) |
| Lateral epicondyle osteotomy | Chevron fragment 4 cm with extensors + LCL → hinge on the intact MCL (Prof Mansour; AO) | Refix with a pre-drilled screw |
| **Boyd** | Along the posterior ulna → anconeus + supinator lifted off as one mass → radial head from behind (Campbell) | **Synostosis** if ulnar periosteum stripped (Prof Mansour; AO) |

[[FIG: Fig 3B.9, 3B.10, 3B.11 · 3B.03

- Stiff elbow (lateral column) → keep the capsular cut **in front of** the LUCL line (Campbell)

CLINICAL PEARL — stiff elbow release
- Flexion lost → **posterior** capsule + MCL posterior band; extension lost → **anterior** capsule + osteophytes (Sport sheet)
- Outerbridge–Kashiwagi → olecranon fossa fenestration (Sport sheet)
- Ulnar symptoms before surgery or flexion <90° → add a medial **ulnar nerve release** (Campbell)

PITFALL — open the joint with varus or valgus?
- After lateral epicondyle osteotomy → L06 says **valgus** to see the medial side; L10 says **varus** for a clearer view (Prof Mansour)
- Hinge on the intact MCL → the lateral side opens with **varus** (AO)
- Say → "varus opens the lateral side; heavy valgus stretches the ulnar nerve"

3B.04.t: Posterior Approach — Skin, Flaps & the Ulnar Nerve
3B.04.b:
### Step by step
1) **Position** → lateral decubitus or prone, arm on a bolster, forearm hanging (Hopp; Campbell)
2) **Incision** → midline ≈15 cm (8 above, 7 below the tip), curved **laterally** → scar off the tip and the ulnar nerve (Prof Mansour; Hopp; Operative sheet)
3) **Flaps** → full-thickness fasciocutaneous, one block → skin and cutaneous nerves safe (Prof Mansour; AO)
4) **Ulnar nerve first** → behind the medial epicondyle, 5–6 cm up and into FCU (flexor carpi ulnaris) to its first motor branch (Prof Mansour; AO)

[[FIG: Fig 3B.12, 3B.13 · 3B.04

- No internervous plane → triceps is radial-supplied **far proximal** (Hopp)
- Keep fat and vessels on the nerve; tapes only to identify, **never to pull** (Hopp; Prof Mansour)
- Going proximal → find the **radial nerve** (spiral groove → lateral IMS), a handbreadth above the epicondyle (Hopp; Prof Mansour)

### In situ or transpose?
| | Evidence (Prof Mansour) |
|---|---|
| Ulnar neuropathy after distal humerus fixation | ≈19%, more after transposition (meta-analysis 2018) |
| In situ vs anterior transposition | **No difference** (Level I RCT 2021) |
| Prof Mansour's practice | ≈99% left in situ; transpose if a medial plate threatens it or in contracture release |
| Implant removal expected | Transpose at closure → safer second operation (Hopp) |

[[FIG: Fig 3B.14 · 3B.04

- Always record the nerve's final position in the operation note (AO)

3B.05.t: Posterior Deep Options — Split, Sparing, Osteotomy
3B.05.b:
### Triceps split & triceps reflection
| Approach | How | Use / limit |
|---|---|---|
| **Triceps split** (Campbell) | Midline split from the tip, 3–4 cm above the fracture (AO) | Extensile; open fractures (spike already through triceps); limited joint view |
| Tongue (V-Y) | Distally based tongue of tendon (Prof Mansour; Campbell) | Lengthens triceps in extension contracture |
| **Bryan-Morrey** | Triceps + ulnar periosteum + anconeus peeled **medial → lateral** (Campbell; AO) | Arthroplasty; weak medial edge → **triceps insufficiency** risk |
| **Paratricipital** (Alonso-Llames) | Medial (ulnar nerve) + lateral (off lateral IMS) windows; insertion intact (Prof Mansour; AO) | Extra-articular and simple intra-articular; poor for coronal shear |
| Lateral paraolecranon (triceps-on) | Split 1 cm lateral to the ulnar border (AO) | Arthroplasty; no triceps repair |
| Anconeus–lateral triceps flap | Central tendon / lateral head → down the Kocher interval → one flap (Prof Mansour) | Central tendon stays on |

[[FIG: Fig 3B.15, 3B.16, 3B.17, 3B.18 · 3B.05

- Triceps blood comes from the front → any split must respect it (Prof Mansour)
- Prof Mansour → starts every distal humerus fracture paratricipital, avoids osteotomy

### Triceps-sparing — the two windows
- Medial window → ulnar nerve mobilised; lateral window → triceps off the lateral IMS, anconeus off the humerus (AO)
  [[FIG: Fig 3B.19, 3B.20 · 3B.05
- More distal view → may cut the MCL **posterior** band, never the anterior band; laterally never the LUCL (AO)
- Reduce → one K-wire articular → metaphysis; check rotation on the olecranon fossa (Prof Mansour)

### Olecranon osteotomy
1) Ulnar nerve out; anconeus off laterally, FCU off medially (Prof Mansour; AO)
2) Find the **bare area** → dissector through the joint or K-wire under fluoroscopy (Prof Mansour; Campbell)
3) **Chevron, apex distal**, ≈60°; drill 2.5 mm at the apex (AO; Campbell)
4) Saw **¾ depth** → crack the rest with an osteotome → jigsaw fit (Campbell; AO)
5) **Pre-drill** the fixation before cutting; long implant (Campbell; Prof Mansour)

[[FIG: Fig 3B.21, 3B.22, 3B.23, 3B.24 · 3B.05

- Best exposure of the articular surface (Wilkinson & Stanley via Campbell); price → a new fracture, hardware irritation (AO)

| Comparison (Prof Mansour) | Result |
|---|---|
| Chevron vs transverse | No difference |
| Step-cut osteotomy | Cadaver only → **do not do it** |
| Triceps tongue vs osteotomy (cadaver 2023; Cleveland cohort 2022) | Same exposure and function; tongue → better motion, less blood loss and ulnar neuritis |
| Osteotomy vs paratricipital (systematic review) | Approach does not change outcome |

MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "posterior approaches to the distal humerus"
- All share **one midline incision**, full-thickness flaps, **ulnar nerve first**
- They differ by the triceps → **split** (Campbell), **reflected** (Bryan-Morrey, tongue), **spared** (paratricipital, triceps-on), **off with bone** (olecranon osteotomy)
- Most exposure → osteotomy; least triceps damage → paratricipital
- Osteotomy → chevron, apex distal, at the bare area, pre-drilled
- Arthroplasty → triceps-on or Bryan-Morrey; never osteotomy (needs the ulna)

3B.07.t: Anterior Approach — Cubital Fossa & Distal Biceps
3B.07.b:
### Step by step
| Step | Anterior (Henry) approach to the cubital fossa |
|---|---|
| Uses | Brachial artery, median and radial nerve repair; **distal biceps**; anterior capsule release (Hopp) |

| Interval | Proximal BR (radial) / brachialis (musculocutaneous); distal BR / PT (median) (Hopp) |
| Superficial | Save the **LABC** (lateral antebrachial cutaneous nerve) between biceps and brachialis; cut the lacertus near the biceps (Hopp) |
| Deep | Supinate → strip the supinator off the radius → capsule (Hopp) |

[[FIG: Fig 3B.29, 3B.30, 3B.31 · 3B.07

- **Recurrent radial vessels** → ligate at once; a retracted bleeder → haematoma → Volkmann contracture (Campbell)

3B.08.t: Forearm — Anterior Approach to the Radius (Henry)
3B.08.b:
### Step by step
| Step | Henry |
|---|---|
| Uses | Whole radius; biceps tuberosity; compartment release (Hopp; AO) |
| Position | Supine, arm board, **supinated**; tourniquet without full exsanguination (Hopp) |
| Incision | Lateral to the biceps tendon at the crease → radial styloid (Hopp) |
| Interval | Distal **BR (radial) / FCR (median)**; proximal **BR / PT** (Hopp) |
| Superficial | Ligate the **recurrent leash**; radial artery medially; superficial radial nerve laterally with BR (Hopp; AO) |

[[FIG: Fig 3B.33, 3B.34, 3B.35 · 3B.08

### Deep by thirds & dangers
| Third | Do this (Hopp; AO) |
|---|---|
| Proximal | **Full supination** → cut the supinator at its insertion, lateral to the biceps → strip laterally (PIN inside it) |
| Middle | **Pronate** → detach PT insertion (keep a cuff) + FDS (flexor digitorum superficialis) origin |
| Distal | Lift **FPL + PQ** (flexor pollicis longus, pronator quadratus) off the radius from the lateral side |

[[FIG: Fig 3B.36, 3B.37, 3B.38 · 3B.08

- **PIN** touches the radial neck in ≈25% → no retractor behind the neck (Hopp)
- Traction neurapraxia of the PIN → recovers in 6–9 months (Hopp)
- Radial artery → under BR mid-forearm; medial to the biceps tendon above → stay lateral (Hopp)

MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "Henry approach"
- **BR / FCR** distally, **BR / PT** proximally → radial vs median nerve
- Leash of Henry ligated; radial artery medial, superficial radial nerve lateral
- Proximal third → **supinate** and strip the supinator from its insertion → PIN protected inside it
- Middle → pronate, detach PT; distal → lift FPL + PQ
- Whole radius, extensile to the wrist and up to the elbow

3B.09.b:
### Thompson
| Step | Thompson |
|---|---|
| Uses | Middle + distal radius (dorsal = tension side); PIN decompression (Hopp; AO) |
| Incision | In front of the lateral epicondyle → ulnar side of Lister's tubercle (Hopp) |
| Interval | Proximal **ECRB (radial) / EDC (PIN)**; distal ECRB / EPL (extensor pollicis longus) (Hopp) |
| Superficial | Start distally at the APL/EPB (abductor pollicis longus / extensor pollicis brevis) crossing → plane is clearer there (Hopp; AO) |
| Deep | Middle third → slide APL/EPB; proximal third → **supinator with the PIN inside** |

[[FIG: Fig 3B.39, 3B.40, 3B.41 · 3B.09

- PIN exits the supinator ≈1 cm above its distal edge (Hopp)
- Full supination brings the supinator into view and moves the PIN away (AO)

PITFALL — protect the PIN in the proximal third
- Hopp → dissect the PIN out **fully** first; it lies on the periosteum in 1 of 4
- Campbell → strip the supinator subperiosteally **with the nerve inside it**
- AO → proximal extension "carries considerable risk" → find the nerve, then strip
- Say → "identify the PIN, then lift the supinator off the bone with the nerve in it"

### Ulna shaft
- **Subcutaneous border**, olecranon → styloid; interval **ECU (PIN) / FCU (ulnar)** (Hopp; AO)
  [[FIG: Fig 3B.42, 3B.43 · 3B.09
- Stay epi-periosteal; near the olecranon → anconeus / FCU (Hopp)
- Proximal fifth → find the **ulnar nerve between the FCU heads** first; distal → dorsal branch of the ulnar nerve (Hopp; AO)
- Swollen forearm → shift the incision onto the extensor muscle → no implant left bare (AO)

EXAM PEARL — pin safe zones in the forearm
- **Ulna** → anywhere along the subcutaneous border, between ECU and FCU (AO)
- **Radius** → dorsal in the middle third, lateral in the distal third; **never anterior** (AO; TRAUMA sheet)
- Proximal third of the radius → PIN under the supinator → avoid (AO)

3B.10.b:
### Supracondylar pinning
1) Gentle traction → correct rotation → mediolateral shift → push the olecranon → flex (Prof Abdel-Ghani)
2) **Lateral wires first** → 2 for Gartland II, 3 for III–IV; spread ≥⅓ of the bone width at the fracture, grip the medial cortex (Prof Abdel-Ghani; Operative sheet)
3) Unstable on testing → **medial pin**: elbow **not fully flexed**, nerve rolled back, 1 cm cut, blunt to bone, enter the **front** of the epicondyle tip (Prof Abdel-Ghani; Operative sheet)

[[FIG: Fig 3B.44 · 3B.10

- Medial pin → ulnar nerve injury ≈3% (3–8%); crossed pins stronger (Prof Abdel-Ghani)
- Pulse lost after reduction → undo, open anteriorly, explore (Prof Abdel-Ghani)

PITFALL — open reduction of a supracondylar fracture
- Prof Abdel-Ghani → **anterior** (removes the obstacle, explores vessels); posterior abandoned
- TRAUMA sheet → **lateral** safest; anterior only for vascular injury; medial risks the ulnar nerve
- Say → "anterior if vessels need exploring, otherwise the side of the spike; never posterior"

### Lateral condyle & neglected Monteggia
| | Lateral condyle ORIF | Neglected Monteggia |
|---|---|---|
| Approach | Lateral, between triceps and the radial wrist extensors | One posterior approach along the ulna |
| Key step | Stay **anterior** → its blood comes from behind (AVN (avascular necrosis), fishtail); arthrotomy just in front of the capitellum; first wire below the epicondyle, parallel to the joint (Operative sheet) | **Ulnar osteotomy first**, overcorrect → head reduces |
| Check | Reduction by the **joint surface**, never the metaphysis | Muscle sleeve lifted with the PIN inside; no Hohmann round the neck |

(Prof Abdel-Ghani)
[[FIG: Fig 3B.45, 3B.46 · 3B.10

- Annular ligament reconstruction → rarely needed after a correct osteotomy (Prof Abdel-Ghani)
- **Medial epicondyle ORIF** → supine, arm externally rotated, incision over the epicondyle (Operative sheet)
- Ulnar nerve found behind it, MABC spared · wires away from the olecranon fossa (Operative sheet)

3B.11.b:
### The sequence & the stability test
- Triad → **posterolateral dislocation + radial head + coronoid** fractures (→ 3A 3.06)
  [[FIG: Fig 3B.47 · 3B.11
- Approach → **Kocher** (lateral), ± medial (FCU split / over-the-top) for the coronoid or MCL (AO; Prof Mansour)
- Repair inside → out: **coronoid → radial head (fix or replace) → LCL** → test → MCL or hinged fixator only if still unstable
  - After repair → stable in all positions = **done** · unstable in supination or both → splint / **MCL** (medial side) → 3A 3.05 (Prof Mansour)
- One lateral epicondyle anchor → holds LUCL + LCL complex + common extensor origin; coronoid sutures tied over the back of the ulna (Operative sheet)
- X-ray check → congruent joint, **equal medial and lateral joint space** (Prof Mansour; Nagah p35)

3B.12.b:
### Total elbow & radial head arthroplasty
| | Total elbow arthroplasty (TEA) | Radial head arthroplasty (RHA) |
|---|---|---|
| Approach | Posterior, incision **just medial to the tip** (Campbell) | Kocher if the LCL is torn; EDC split / Kaplan if intact (Campbell) |
| Triceps | **Triceps-on** (paratricipital / paraolecranon) or Bryan-Morrey off; same results → Campbell prefers triceps-on | — |
| Nerve | **Ulnar nerve transposed** anteriorly (Campbell) | PIN → pronate |
| Key point | Release both collaterals to dislocate | **No overstuffing** → head level with the lateral coronoid edge |

[[FIG: Fig 3B.48, 3B.49, 3B.50 · 3B.12

- TEA complications → **ulnar neuritis** (≈11% paraesthesia) and triceps insufficiency (Campbell)
- Triceps detached → no active extension for 3 months, lift ≤5 lb (Campbell)
- RHA → >2 mm too long → radiocapitellar overload; **lateral ulnohumeral gap** shows it (Campbell)
- TEA wound → dress at ≈60° flexion → the olecranon tip stays off the incision (Campbell)

PITFALL — which interval for a radial head prosthesis?
- Hopp → Kocher for all radial head surgery
- Campbell → EDC split / Kaplan if the LUCL is intact, Kocher if torn
- Say → "use the interval the injury opened; repair the LUCL to its isometric point"

### Arthrodesis
- Approach → posterior, ulnar nerve isolated, triceps split + extended paraolecranon; posterior humeral plate under compression (Campbell)
  [[FIG: Fig 3B.51 · 3B.12
- Position → one side **90–100°** (grip); both sides → one 110–120° (mouth), one 45–65° (hygiene) (Campbell)
- Keep rotation → resect the radial head if needed; implants out no earlier than 18 months (Campbell)
